a-morning-walk-woman-golden-retriever-qu:
A morning walk. Woman, golden retriever, quiet suburban park. Nothing happens except a dog being a dog. And the beat that sells the whole thing is him not quite finishing the fetch.

Most people write vlog prompts where everything goes right. Real footage is full of small failures nobody edits out, and that's precisely what makes it read as real rather than staged.

Here's the full prompt:

CAMERA: Handheld DV 16mm daily vlog footage. The video MUST begin with her holding the camera at arm's length in selfie mode while stepping outside her apartment building with her dog. The first 20–30 seconds are entirely handheld. Later she occasionally places the camera on a park bench, low stone wall, picnic table, or the ground for wider shots. Keep subtle handheld shake, drifting composition, autofocus hunting, rushed reframing, uneven zooms, exposure breathing, brief accidental face cropping, and imperfect framing throughout. The camera itself is never visible.

LOOK: Warm analog tape texture with gentle film grain, slightly softened sharpness, subtle halation around sunlight, realistic skin tones, low contrast, tiny exposure shifts, and natural motion blur. Authentic footage from someone's everyday life rather than a polished commercial.

STYLE: A relaxed morning lifestyle vlog. Quiet, cozy, spontaneous. She occasionally laughs at her dog, pauses to look around, adjusts the leash, brushes hair away from her face, and speaks naturally in short sentences with comfortable pauses.

CHARACTER: EMMA, mid-20s. Long light brown hair in a messy ponytail, green eyes, minimal makeup, oversized gray hoodie, black biker shorts, white sneakers, small crossbody bag. Walking a happy golden retriever.

SETTING: A peaceful suburban neighborhood on a sunny morning. Tree-lined sidewalks, quiet residential streets, birds singing, a small park with benches, green grass, soft golden morning light. Very few people around.

SCENES: Opens in selfie mode, leaving the apartment building, dog pulling excitedly on the leash. "Good morning." Smiles. "Someone couldn't wait." The dog sniffs everything as they walk. Quiet laugh. "He has to inspect every single tree." Still handheld, into a small park. The dog stops and stares at a squirrel. "Oh... there we go." Small headshake. She sets the camera on a bench for a wider angle and throws a tennis ball. The dog chases it. "Worth waking up early." Picks the camera back up, walking slowly, looks up at the trees. "It's actually really peaceful out here." The dog returns with the ball but drops it halfway. She laughs. "Close enough." She sits on the bench, dog lying beside her, scratching behind his ears. "I think he's happier than I am." Stands, keeps walking, selfie mode heading home. "Coffee is definitely next." Smiles into the lens. "See you later." Small wave, ends the recording.

A few things worth noticing about why it's built this way:

The dog is the unpredictability engine. Stopping at a squirrel, dropping the ball halfway, inspecting every tree. An animal doing animal things gives the scene a randomness that a scripted human beat never would.

The camera gets put down and picked back up. Handheld, then propped on a bench for the wide, then handheld again. That rhythm is what an actual vlogger does, and it's why the wide shots don't feel like a different production.

Every line is four words or fewer. "Close enough." "Worth waking up early." Nobody narrates in full sentences while walking a dog.

And the camera block is a list of mistakes on purpose. Autofocus hunting, accidental face cropping, drifting composition. Every one is a flaw, and every one is doing the heavy lifting.

Seedance 2.5 handled it clean. The tech isn't the limiting factor anymore, asking it to look imperfect is.

Critically they are OCCLUDED by real objects in front of them, so a passing umbrella hides part of a bounding box and reveals it on the far side, and rain falls in front of every line. The interface has NO glow, emits no light, casts no shadow and does not reflect in the road.

THE EFFECTS RULE: every change lands on the real world physically. A rotated building is a real building at that angle with a correctly rotated shadow. A faded crowd is genuinely semi-transparent with the road visible through them. A masked region is real daylight on real dry ground. Nothing pops, flashes, sparkles or glows. Changes land in a single frame or over a smooth drag, never with an effect.

Base environment: photoreal cinematic, anamorphic, shallow focus, 35mm grain, practical light only. Everything wet and mirrored. Never stylised, never fantasy, never science fiction. Apart from the vector overlay this is a documentary photograph of a wet city at night.

Shot language: ONE CONTINUOUS TAKE, no hard cuts. A single very slow arc around her, from past her left shoulder to past her right across the full thirty seconds, so the perspective on every interface element changes continuously.

Performance core: she is not performing power, she is doing work. No flourishes, no hero poses, no glance at the lens. Pedestrians never react, never look at her and never break stride.

Inside the masked rectangle: flat overcast midday, soft, shadowless, dry pale tarmac. The two meet on a razor-sharp vertical line with no blend and no spill.

Her soaked coat swings with delay. The rotating tower has enormous mass and structural inertia. The bus sheds water in sheets. Reversed time reverses everything at the same rate.

This didn't need confusing AI prompts, it's made with 10 second clips spliced together, a starting image and a character reference.

The prompt for each 10 seconds was a paragraph of text very basically describing the scene

I'm not here to show you a fully polished, no error clip as that's not a real representation of todays AI.

Photoreal live sports broadcast. Shallow depth of field on close shots, deep
focus on wides. Hard key from stadium floodlights overhead. Strong rim light
separating the runners from the dark crowd. Thousands of camera flashes
popping across the stands as a moving field of white specks.

Broadcast telephoto and trackside rail cameras. Exactly ONE camera move per
time slice. Never combine moves.

the real fine pores and natural skin texture. Long neck, broad flat
shoulders, very long legs, narrow hips, deep chest, long muscle bellies
rather than bulk. Sharp cheekbones, jaw clenched at the start, eyes locked

with a close fade. Yellow-and-green singlet, bib number 4. Veins raised on

individually, never in focus. Shorter, more compact builds. Higher stride
frequency, choppier. Mixed dark and light singlets.
Crowd: an undifferentiated mass, out of focus, rising to their feet in a wave.

PERFORMANCE CORE
The story is the delay and the release. He is level with the field for the
first third, then unfolds and eats the gap alive. Show dominance through
stride length and empty track, not through slow-motion tricks.

FORBIDDEN
No subtitles. No captions. No on-screen graphics, scoreboard, timer, or any
legible text or numbers. No commentator voice. No dialogue of any kind. No
background music. No runners appearing or vanishing — exactly eight on the

not change between shots. No flickering limbs, no duplicated arms or legs,
no warped feet.

0-2s / Frame 0-48 — THE STILLNESS
Action: Eight sprinters in the set position, hips high, fingertips on the
  line. Hero in lane 4, center frame — even folded into the blocks he is
  obviously the longest body in the row, knees stacked higher than anyone

Negative: no subtitles, no music.

Sound: Crowd roar detonating, spikes ripping rubber, explosive breathing.
Negative: no subtitles, no music, no commentator.

Action: He finally comes to full upright posture, later than everyone else —
  and the stride opens to its full length. Each contact now swallows the
  ground the others need two steps for. At 45 meters he draws level and goes
  past. Sweat flies off his shoulders in visible droplets, catching the
  floodlights. By 60 meters he is two body lengths clear.
Intent: The moment the race stops being a race.
Camera: Long telephoto, head-on from the finish line. ONE slow push in.
  Compressed perspective stacks the pack behind him.
Sound: Sustained roar building, a rolling wall of sound.
Negative: no subtitles, no music.

Action: His face settles into the top-end sprint mask — jaw loose, cheeks

  ground. Clean empty track between him and the nearest rival, about four
  meters. Heat haze distorting the air in that gap.
Intent: Let the empty track do the work.
Camera: Low tracking rail alongside the hero. ONE steady lateral move.
Sound: Crowd at a continuous peak, breathing, spikes.
Negative: no subtitles, no music.

Frame 274 (11.4s) — THE LINE
Action: Chest hits the line. Torso dips hard. Long arms flung back. The

Camera: Side-on at the finish. Drop to slow motion for a beat, then return

Sound: The roar cresting into a single detonation.

Camera: Wide, ONE slow pull back to reveal the full straight.
Sound: Roar, then a ragged edge of disbelief in it.

13-15s — ECSTASY
Action: He wheels around, both long arms flung wide, mouth open in a roar

Camera: Handheld, tight, moving with him. ONE move, following.
Sound: Crowd at maximum. A solid wall of sound with no gaps in it.
Negative: no subtitles, no music, no commentator voice.

telephoto broadcast look. Hero in lane 4 always weighted toward frame center,
always the tallest figure on the track, always taking longer strides than
anyone around him. Keep his face, hair, build, and yellow-and-green singlet
identical in every shot. Keep exactly eight runners on the track the entire
time. No subtitles, no captions, no on-screen text or numbers, no commentator
voice, no dialogue, no background music. Sound is crowd, spikes, breathing,
and the starter's pistol only.

The entire film follows one ordinary handmade paper boat on an impossible journey. There is exactly ONE impossible element in the world: this small paper boat can travel wherever connected water flows, no matter how far. Everything else obeys real-world physics.

Natural child delivery, soft voice, tiny pause between words, no theatrical acting.

His shirt moves with his running.

Small droplets strike the camera lens.

The camera drops almost to water level and begins following the paper boat.

The boat enters a narrow concrete drainage channel.

The boy runs alongside it for a few seconds before stopping.

His expression changes from excitement to concern as the boat disappears into the channel.

changing sunlight,
changing ocean conditions,
different coastlines appearing and disappearing in the distance.

He looks up.

He doesn't react dramatically.

First curiosity.

Then confusion.

Then recognition.

His breathing pauses for a moment.

His eyes soften.

Everything in the film must look completely real except for the single impossible rule governing the paper boat.

NO:

glowing objects,
portals,

卓球・オリンピック決勝 × カンフー映画の高速バトル

【SUMMARY】
10 seconds, 16:9. The final point of an Olympic table tennis final, shot like a Hong Kong
kung fu duel. Two players, one ball, a dark arena, one column of light on the table.
Real time on every impact, deep slow motion between, one burst of pure hyper-speed.

【SET】
A packed arena, the crowd sunk into near-blackness — silhouettes and tiny out-of-focus
highlights. A hard column of white light falls onto a dark blue table with crisp white
lines. Fine dust drifts inside the beams. Extremely realistic physical texture: paddle
rubber, sweat-soaked fabric, the matte ball. High contrast, deep shadow, hard rim light
from above and behind, shallow depth of field around f/2.0.
A physical LED scoreboard hangs in the darkness behind the table, orange digits reading
10 - 10, sharp and correctly formed, never changing. It is the only lettering in the film.

【PLAYERS — two people, never more】
RED: a 24-year-old East Asian man, lean, heavy shoulders and forearms. Cropped black hair
soaked to his forehead. Sharp narrow eyes, high cheekbones, hard jaw. Cool-toned skin with
real pores, wet with sweat. Plain solid red sleeveless shirt, plain black shorts, no logo
or number. The aggressor.
BLUE: a 26-year-old East Asian man, taller and rangier. Longer black hair pushed back,
dripping. Thick brows, square jaw, steady unblinking stare. Warm-toned skin with real
pores. Plain solid blue sleeveless shirt, plain black shorts, no logo or number. The
counter-puncher.
Neither shows fear: two masters at the end of a long duel, calm and spent. The violence is
in the ball, not their faces.

【TIMELINE】

0.0-2.5s SERVE — deep slow motion.
RED tosses the ball straight up. It climbs through the light, turning slowly, dust around
it. He exhales, drops his shoulder, loads his arm. At 2.2s he strikes: real time snaps in
and the ball tears out of frame.
Camera: low angle just above the table surface, looking up past the net. Locked off.
Audio: near silence — his breath, shoes creaking, a low hush. Then one sharp crack.

2.5-4.3s HYPER-SPEED RALLY — no slow motion at all, the fastest passage in the film.
Fourteen exchanges in under two seconds, faster than any real rally. The ball stops
reading as an object and becomes a white streak cutting a line through the dust. Paddle
arms blur into afterimages, shoulders whip, feet smear. Sweat is thrown off both men in
sheets. The table shudders.
Camera: side-on at net height, one smooth horizontal slide along the table — the camera
stays calm while everything inside the frame is violent.
Audio: the cracks run together into a hard stutter like a drum roll, over squealing shoes
and a rising crowd.

4.3-5.5s THE BREATH — the speed drops out.
One exchange stretched into deep slow motion. RED drives the ball low across the net,
sweat lifting off his forearm and floating, dust turning around the ball. BLUE's eyes
track it. At 5.4s his paddle meets it and real time cracks back in.
Camera: the same side-on slide, now crawling.
Audio: everything falls to a muffled rumble and one long breath, then the crack.

5.5-8.0s THE ANSWER — the deepest slow motion in the film.
BLUE pushes off the floor and leaps sideways, body fully extended, back arched, paddle arm
cocked behind his head. He hangs there. Sweat droplets float around him. Dust turns in the
beam. His eyes lock on the ball. At 7.8s the paddle connects and real time slams back with
the loudest crack yet.
Camera: low angle, looking steeply up at him against the black arena roof. Locked off.
Audio: sound drops muffled and distant while he hangs, then the crack at full volume.

8.0-10.0s THE POINT — real time.
The ball skips off the far corner and away into the dark. RED is caught frozen mid-reach,
unable to follow it. BLUE lands hard, skids on one foot, and roars, head back, fists
clenched. Behind them the crowd erupts, thousands of silhouettes rising at once.
Camera: wide on the table and both men, pushing in 5% at most. Hold to the last frame.
Audio: the crowd explodes, his roar cutting through it, the ball still bouncing underneath.

【RECAP — all 10 seconds】
Dark arena, one hard column of light on the dark blue table, drifting dust, a near-black
crowd of silhouettes.
Only two people in frame. Their faces, hair and clothing stay identical in every shot,
every garment a single solid colour with no logo, number or pattern.
One camera movement per shot, never two. Hard clean cuts on impact. The ball stays inside
the frame at all times.
Real time on every impact, deep slow motion between, switching instantly, with one
sustained hyper-speed burst where the ball is a streak.
The scoreboard reads 10 - 10 and never changes, and it is the only lettering.
The sound is the ball, the shoes, the breathing and the crowd — keep the mix free of music
and commentary.

META

STYLE
Black-and-white 35mm arthouse cinema, 1960s European café-film look. High-contrast monochrome, soft film grain, gentle bloom on the lamps, shallow depth of field on close-ups.

LIGHT
Night interior lit only by practicals: hanging globe lamps, the espresso machine's glow, and cold light through the window from the lunar plain. Soft key from the window side, deep shadow in the corners, clear catch-lights in the eyes.

COLOR
None. Full grayscale, rich mid-grays on skin, no tint of any kind.

TEXTURE
Fine grain. Chrome holds soft rolling reflections, glass refracts the lamps in small bright points, skin keeps visible pore-level texture with no smoothing.

MOOD
Quiet, intimate, unhurried — a conversation overheard in a place that is ordinary to the people in it.

SCENE CONTEXT
A near-empty late-night café on the surface of the moon. A man and a woman sit across a small round table beside the wide window, talking about the water. Neither of them ever looks outside.

CHARACTERS

The woman: early thirties, dark bob haircut, intelligent face, dark turtleneck with the cuffs visible at her wrists, thin earrings, light coat over her chair. She sits camera-left. Identical in every shot.

The man: mid-thirties, dark slightly messy hair, light stubble, shadowed under-eyes, dark jacket over an open-collar light shirt, jacket sleeve visible at his wrists. He sits camera-right. Identical in every shot.

LOCATION MAP
Foreground: their small round table. Her espresso cup and the single tall glass of water sit on her side, close to her right hand. His espresso cup and spoon sit on his side. Nothing else on the table.
Midground: small round tables, worn tiled floor, hanging globe lamps, chrome espresso machine at the counter.
Background: a wide window along the wall beside them. Beyond the glass, a grey lunar plain with low craters, black sky, and Earth small and low near the horizon.

FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Interior medium two-shot, 47°, eye level. The woman sits camera-left, the man camera-right, the window and lunar plain behind them, café interior deeper in the room. Her hands are around her cup with the water glass beside it, his forearms rest on the table.

FORMAT MODE
Timed multishot with HARD CUTS only at 6.0s, 8.5s, 11.0s, 13.0s, 16.0s, 19.0s, 22.5s, 25.0s and 28.0s. The camera cuts only at these points.

STORYBOARD

SHOT 1 (0.0–6.0s)
Medium two-shot, 47°, faint 1–2 cm breathing drift.
The woman, eyes on him: "Do you think people get more honest when they're tired?"
The man answers late, eyes coming up off the table: "No. Their lies just get less inventive."

SHOT 2 (6.0–8.5s)
Extreme close-up, 12°, of the woman's hands on her side of the table, dark turtleneck cuffs at her wrists. Her fingers leave her cup, lift the tall glass of water, and set it back down in the same place, the water rocking once.
The woman, speaking over the image: "It's different tonight."

SHOT 3 (8.5–11.0s)
Close portrait of the man, 18°, eyes down.
The man: "They changed the water."

SHOT 4 (11.0–13.0s)
Extreme close-up, 12°, of the man's hand on his side of the table, dark jacket sleeve at his wrist, turning his spoon a half-turn on the saucer.
The woman, speaking over the image from off-frame: "Again?"

SHOT 5 (13.0–16.0s)
Medium close-up of the man, 29°, lunar plain soft behind his shoulder, eyes still on his cup.
The man: "The old one remembered too much."

SHOT 6 (16.0–19.0s)
Close-up of the woman, 18°. Her eyes come up and hold his.
The woman: "Water can't remember people."

SHOT 7 (19.0–22.5s)
Medium close-up of the man, 29°. He swallows once, then looks up at her.
The man: "Probably not. But people can't remember the past either."

SHOT 8 (22.5–25.0s)
Medium two-shot, 47°, lunar plain behind them. She leans in slightly.
The woman: "Then what do we remember?"

SHOT 9 (25.0–28.0s)
Close portrait of the man, 18°. One breath, then his eyes come up and hold hers.
The man: "The last version we could live with."

SHOT 10 (28.0–30.0s)
Close-up of the woman, 18°, the lunar plain and black sky soft behind her through the glass. No dialogue. Her face stills, one slow blink, her eyes drop toward her cup and then drift slightly aside. The shot holds on her to the last frame, the image staying full and lit.

Both faces stay mostly still, so small movements read. Emotion comes through eyelids, brow corners, jaw and breath rather than expression. Blinks work as punctuation — withheld through the important lines, released after. She runs from light and half-joking, to quieter, to genuinely curious, to quiet recognition at the end. Steam curls off the cups and the espresso machine. Water rocks and settles in the glass. The cup meets the saucer with weight, the spoon rings faintly on chrome. Nothing beyond the window moves.

AUDIO
The low hum of an enclosed room, a faint air-system whisper, the hiss of the espresso machine, a spoon against a saucer, a swallow of water. No music anywhere. Voices sit close and dry, as in a small room late at night.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
Black and white throughout, real-time, no slow motion.

POSITIVE LOCKS
The image stays fully monochrome in every shot.

The single glass of water stays on the woman's side of the table for the whole scene, and only she touches it.
